resources.string: Hold a volume key to talk to Claude while Walkie-Claudie is on. Short presses still change the volume. Also logs key presses for the button test.

BUTTON TEST — newest presses on top. Screenshot this screen when done.
1. Turn the walkie off first (main screen › Off), then tap [Start listening] (earphone buttons).
2. Earphone button: single / double / long press — here, on the home screen, with the screen off, inside another app.
3. Volume long-press: [Accessibility] › installed apps › Walkie-Claudie › on. Greyed out? [App info] › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings, then retry.
That isn\'t complete pairing text. Run /walkie:pair on the PC and copy the whole {"url":…,"key":…} line.
Not a Walkie-Claudie QR. Run /walkie:pair on the PC.
Walkie check. Can you hear me clearly?
Down: talk while held. Up: monologue on/off. Screen on only
Playing music hands it to the music app. Long-press the floating button to take it back
Tap to talk, long-press to take the earphone button back
Playing music hands it to the music app. Turn the walkie off and on to take it back
Uses the earphone next-track signal. Skipping songs won\'t work while on
See which key presses reach the app
No channel is open. Start a walkie session on the PC
Reads replies from every open channel; other channels\' replies start with a switch tone. You still talk on the current channel
A reply from another channel switches to it, so your next message goes there too

Walkie-Claudie uses these. Tap Allow in the windows that follow.

· Microphone (required): hears you and turns your speech into text with the phone's speech recognition. Only the text goes to the PC.
· Notifications (recommended): shows an "on" notification while the walkie is on, so you can tell at a glance. It still works if you say no.

When you tap [On], it also walks you through "Display over other apps" (for the floating button) and, for the volume keys, Accessibility.
Without the microphone you can\'t talk.\n\n[App info] below › Permissions › Microphone › Allow only while using the app.

The floating button (the small walkie over other apps) needs the "Display over other apps" permission.

1. [Open settings] below (if a list of apps appears, pick Walkie-Claudie)
2. Turn the switch on (the name varies by phone, e.g. "Allow display over other apps", "Appear on top")
3. Come back and tap [On] again

Not using the floating button? Tap [Turn on without it], or switch it off under Settings › Floating button.
Turn on Accessibility for the volume keys

Hold volume down to talk and volume up for monologue mode: both need Walkie-Claudie's accessibility service, because Android only hands volume key presses to other apps through Accessibility. It watches the volume keys only; it doesn't read the screen.

How
1. [Accessibility] below
2. Installed apps › Walkie-Claudie (the menu name varies by phone, e.g. "Downloaded apps", "Installed services")
3. Turn the switch on › Allow (the "full control" warning is the same for every accessibility app)

Switch greyed out, or a "Restricted setting" message? (Android 13+, apps installed outside the Play Store)
1. [App info] below › ⋮ (top right) › Allow restricted settings
2. Back to [Accessibility] and turn it on

Not using the volume keys? [Later]. The floating and earphone buttons work without it.
The volume keys need it on
Without the Bluetooth permission only wired and USB headset mics can be used; a Bluetooth headset falls back to the default mic.
Tap to switch: Auto (system default), Phone (built-in mic), Headset (wired, USB or Bluetooth). Falls back to the default if the headset isn\'t connected
Tap to switch: Pause (music stops, then resumes), Duck (music gets quieter), Off. Applies while you record and while a reply is read aloud
Check that the selected mic hears you
Tap Start, say a sentence, then tap Stop. Nothing is sent to the PC
The mic test needs Android 13 or newer, like monologue mode
The walkie is recording or a call is on. Try again afterwards
Sound was picked up, but no words were recognised. Speak closer or clearer
No sound picked up. Check the mic choice in Settings, or that the headset is connected
